mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% over the last three months indicates a tightening labor market, which can lead to increased wage pressures and inflation, causing the S&P 500 to experience negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3% in the last three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS showed a sustained increase over the last three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the last month indicates a surge in supply-side activity, which can lead to increased productivity and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it indicates a strong labor market recovery, boosting consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS increase > 200k in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE was above 6% and PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which can lead to a broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST decreased by more than 5% in the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it indicates inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to potential monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over the last five months signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 showed a sustained increase over the last five months.
